traits.fan_split_depth.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 274): the blade regularly divided to below the middle into single-fold segments, so the splits run from the edge past the blade's middle; read as free over 0.55 to 0.75 of their length.

traits.segment_posture.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 274): narrow stiff segments, shortly bifid.

traits.segment_filaments.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 274) names no threads between or on the segments.

traits.petiole_armature.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 274): the petiole's margins armed with numerous small teeth; drawn at the family's size and spacing for fine teeth, as no size is given.

traits.petiole_tooth_form.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 274): small teeth, no curve named; drawn square to the petiole.

traits.petiole_teeth_distal.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 274): numerous small teeth along the margin, no change toward the blade named; drawn even.

traits.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under the genus (Palmae III 4b): S. repens, a colonial, nearly stemless palm with bisexual flowers and toothed petiole margins, often forming thickets.

traits.leaf_division.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments: simple, parted, palmate.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments: simple, parted, palmate.

traits.division_pattern.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. traits.clonal.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: it grows in clusters of stems; its dead leaves stay on the stem (marcescent) rather than falling cleanly.

generator.params.skirt.why: Dead fronds hang on the stem instead of falling.

generator.params.dead_life.why: How many years a dead frond hangs, set by eye: the book says only that they stay on, and most such palms shed them within a few years (the California fan palm, whose skirt lasts for decades, sets its own).

generator.params.dead_angle.why: A dead frond hangs close against the stem, as the built-in California fan palm's do.

rules.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: it grows in clusters of stems; its dead leaves stay on the stem (marcescent) rather than falling cleanly.

appearance.note: A dead frond drawn as the built-in palms draw theirs: a brown fan for a fan palm, a brown feather frond for a feather palm.
